svg.aria-label: How to write 请: 10 strokes · 9 pen lifts · 14 movements
svg.title: Writing 请
svg.desc: 14 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 请 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 请.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E8%AF%B7.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 请. Medians 1–2 draw 讠: a down-right dot, then a separately started short horizontal that turns down and finishes up-right without lifting. Medians 3–10 draw 青: two upper horizontals, a central vertical, a wide middle horizontal, the lower left side, a separately started lower top horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks left at the base without lifting, then two inner horizontals. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all ten medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all four internal turns across 讠 and 青, and nine intervening lifts; Noto's 青 horizontals are flatter and its lower enclosure is squarer than the Arphic-derived source graphic.
